cautions: Copyright and trademark pervade this subject. Visual works, photographs, typefaces/font files, and logos are protected. Describe design principles and NAME works and designers; never reproduce a copyrighted image, logo, font file, or proprietary color specification. Pantone colors and named brand palettes are proprietary — REFERENCE_ONLY, do not reproduce values. Use CC0/public-domain or originally-described examples.

Design 'rules' are conventions and heuristics, not laws. Present the rule of thirds, the golden ratio, and grid systems as useful conventions with limits. The claim that the golden ratio explains great design or appears throughout nature/art is frequently overstated — attribute such claims and note the skepticism rather than asserting them.

Color psychology and color 'meanings' are culturally contingent and weakly evidenced. Present them as design convention and cultural association, not as established science, and note cross-cultural variation.

Copyright, fair use, and licensing are legal topics — teach the concepts from the U.S. Copyright Office and cite it, but state clearly that fair use is fact-specific and that the lesson is educational, not legal advice. Distinguish copyright from trademark, licensing models (rights-managed vs royalty-free), and the role of model/property releases.

Creative Commons: describe the six licenses and CC0 exactly as Creative Commons defines them (the BY/SA/NC/ND elements), including that CC licenses are irrevocable and apply on top of copyright. Do not conflate 'Creative Commons' with 'public domain' or 'free of all restrictions'.

Accessibility claims must match WCAG. Cite the real thresholds (contrast 4.5:1 for normal text, 3:1 for large text and UI components under WCAG 2.1 AA), the don't-rely-on-color-alone rule, and text alternatives. Attribute to the W3C WAI.

Technical values are conventions with reasons: '300 dpi for print' and '72 ppi' legacy screen resolution should be explained (why), and modern screen density (device pixels/PPI) noted. Distinguish ppi from dpi, resolution from dimensions, and raster from vector accurately.

Describe software categories and techniques generically; do not endorse specific commercial products, reproduce proprietary UI, or present one tool as required. Digital-media technical facts (frame rates, codecs, aspect ratios, file formats) should be sourced and accurate.
Distribute question answer keys EVENLY across A/B/C/D — aim for a balanced spread across the whole subject without singling out any one position.
